content: 1. Elvitegravir is no longer available in the United States as a single drug. 2. Co-administration of cobicistat, a strong CYP3A4 and BCRP inhibitor, increases duvelisib levels, which may elevate the risk of duvelisib toxicities. The duvelisib dose should be reduced to 15 mg BID when co-administered with cobicistat. 3. Elvitegravir increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Ribociclib increases elvitegravir levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Elvitegravir increases adagrasib levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If unavoidable, adagrasib concentrations should reach steady-state (~8 days) before co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 6. Apalutamide decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administration is necessary, evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as per prescribing information. 7. Antiretroviral (ART) medications may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. ARTs should not be taken for at least 1 month before cell mobilization or the expected duration for elimination of the medications. 8. ARTs may also interfere with the manufacturing of betibeglogene autotemcel. ARTs should be discontinued for at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 9. Bosentan decreases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 10. Carbamazepine decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 11. Copanlisib levels are increased by elvitegravir through CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, the copanlisib dose should be reduced to 45 mg. 12. Dabrafenib decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 13. Dexamethasone decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 14. Efavirenz decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 15. Elivaldogene autotemcel manufacturing may be interfered with by ARTs. ARTs should be discontinued for at least 1 month before initiating stem cell mobilization medications and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 16. Enzalutamide decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 17. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 18. Ethinyl estradiol levels are decreased by elvitegravir through an unknown mechanism. Alternative non-hormonal contraceptive methods should be considered. 19. Etravirine increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 20. Fexinidazole increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Co-administration may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 21. Fosphenytoin decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 22. Infigratinib levels are increased by elvitegravir through CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 23. Lovotibeglogene autotemcel manufacturing may be interfered with by ARTs. ARTs should be discontinued for at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 24. Mifepristone increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 25. Mitotane decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 26. Nafcillin decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 27. Nevirapine decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 28. Oxcarbazepine decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 29. Pentobarbital decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 30. Phenobarbital decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 31. Phenytoin decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 32. Primidone decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 33. Rifabutin decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 34. Rifampin decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 35. Rifapentine decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 36. St. John’s Wort decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 37. Tucatinib increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of the CYP3A substrate according to product labeling. 38. Aluminum hydroxide decreases elvitegravir levels by cation binding in the GI tract. Separate the dose of elvitegravir from antacids by at least 2 hours. 39. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases elvitegravir levels by cation binding in the GI tract. Separate the dose of elvitegravir from antacids by at least 2 hours. 40. Atazanavir increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. The recommended dose is elvitegravir 85 mg PO once daily with atazanavir/ritonavir. 41. Belzutifan decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. 42. Calcium carbonate decreases elvitegravir levels by cation binding in the GI tract. Separate the dose of elvitegravir from antacids by at least 2 hours. 43. Cenobamate decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate as needed when co-administered with cenobamate. 44. Clarithromycin increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Conivaptan increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Danazol increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Darunavir may increase elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
